newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BM&F to launch alcohol contract in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BM&F to launch alcohol contract in Q1.

text.p: Brazilian futures exchange Bolsa de Mercadorias & Futuros (BM&F) plans to launch alcohol futures contracts in the first quarter of 1997, said a top bolsa official.
"The contract has already been approved by the government and we are likely to launch it in the first quarter," said Manoel Felix Cintra Neto, the new BM&F president, without giving further details.
Cintra Neto, who will be elected by the bolsa's Board of Directors Tuesday for a one-year term, will replace Manoel Pires da Costa who headed BM&F for five years.
Cintra Neto said BM&F in 1997 will focus on developing new products, particularly agricultural contracts, and increasing the participation of foreign investors in the futures markets.

"We want to develop new agricultural contracts to offer more hedge instruments for Brazilian producers," he told reporters, adding that Brazil's agricultural sector is primarily financed by what he called traditional financing instruments.
Departing president Manoel Pires da Costa also emphasized the BM&F's plans to continue developing new contracts to meet the demands of the agricultural sector.
He said agricultural contracts surged 156 percent last year over 1995 and still have room to grow.
BM&F ended 1996 with a daily financial volume of $19 billion. Total volume last year was $4.8 trillion, up more than 50 percent from roughly $3.0 trillion in 1995.
The bolsa launched eight new contracts, including foreign debt, cotton and corn contracts.
The exchange ended the year with a net worth of $335 million, up from $31 million in December 1991.
